issues.description: Close message type is 'Close' but PR claims it should be 'CloseStream'
issues.detail: The PR description and Deepgram docs say the control message is {"type": "CloseStream"}, but the code sends {"type": "Close"}. That's the entire point of the patch. Either the description is wrong or the code is wrong; one of them gets fixed before this lands. Verify against the Speak v1 socket client and resubmit with the correct string.

issues.description: Single ws.receive() with 1s timeout is not 'wait for final messages'
issues.detail: Deepgram can emit multiple frames (audio + Flushed + Closed) after Flush/Close. A single receive() grabs one message and returns. If you actually want to drain, loop until you see the Closed ack or the socket closes, bounded by the timeout. As written, the 'race condition' comment overstates what the code does.

issues.description: Bare Exception swallow hides protocol bugs behind a warning
issues.detail: Catching Exception around send_str/receive will silently eat ConnectionResetError, CancelledError, and anything else. CancelledError in particular must be re-raised or the task cancellation semantics break. Narrow the except to the connection-level errors you actually expect, and let the rest propagate.

issues.description: THREE-PATCHES: Flush, Close, and drain-wait are three changes in one diff
issues.detail: Sending Flush, sending Close, and adding a receive-with-timeout are three distinct behavioral changes. The commit message and title only mention CloseStream. If Flush regresses something, bisect points at one commit doing three things. Split into separate patches or at minimum justify Flush in the message.

issues.description: f-string in logger.warning instead of lazy formatting
issues.detail: Minor, but the surrounding codebase conventions for logging usually prefer logger.warning('msg %s', e) so the format cost is skipped when the level is disabled. Not a hill to die on, but match the house style.

review.summary: Verdict: NEEDS-WORK. The intent is right and the STT-alignment argument is sound, but the patch ships a message type ('Close') that contradicts the PR description and the Deepgram docs it cites ('CloseStream') — that alone refuses the patch until reconciled. Beyond that, the 'wait for final messages' is a single receive() with a bare-Exception swallow, which is not actually draining and will hide cancellation. This is really three changes (Flush, Close, drain) sold as one. Fix the message string, narrow the except, loop the drain, and it lands.
